exposure: mode of delivery (vaginal vs. cesarean) in multiple births
finding: While large retrospective cohort studies from the 1990s suggested an increased risk of mortality and morbidity for the second twin in vaginal births, the 2013 prospective, multi-center randomized Twin Birth Study found no difference in outcomes between planned vaginal and cesarean births under optimum conditions.
mod_finding: The Twin Birth Study, a prospective, multi-center randomized study, found no difference in neonatal and maternal mortality and morbidity between planned vaginal birth and planned cesarean birth in multiple pregnancies under optimal conditions.
